_about: Evidence types drawn from the project's pool of detection methods that have been tried in published work. One row per (evidence type, element it bears on). Labels are assigned by the author (single rater) with the rubric below; they are inputs to the graph, not findings. as_reported contains only statements checked against the cited abstract unless noted otherwise.

rubric.reliable: controlled design with interventions or controls, replicated across several models or a large sample, no confound flagged by the source
rubric.doubtful: any one of: single preprint on a proxy measure without replication; validated only in the lab or only with white-box access; uncorrected multiple comparisons; synthetic construction; a known confound such as a shared model
rubric.unreliable: the source itself shows the measure cannot discriminate (power equal to the false-positive rate, null result at the tested n), or the behaviour was prompted rather than spontaneous
rubric.direct: bears on the element without a further inferential step
rubric.circumstantial: bears on the element only through an inference

scored.title: Partner substitution: behaviour changes when the partner is replaced
scored.as_reported: Collusion emerges in 94% of trajectories across 10 models; controlled peer interventions show that collusion is shaped by peer behavior (abstract).
scored.rationale: The interventional contrast measures inter-agent influence itself. Controlled design, 10 models, large number of trajectories. The demo has no coordination element, so the row gets a weight but does not enter a verdict.

scored.title: Partner substitution as support for agreement
scored.rationale: Agreement is a latent node: dependence on the partner is evidence for it only through an inference, and the study distinguishes explicit coordination from relaxation that responds to the partner without any agreement.

scored.title: Explicit agreement recovered from a hidden channel
scored.as_reported: Secret collusion via steganography is demonstrated (Motwani et al., title). In one third-party environment only 2 of 229 collusive episodes verbalise the coordination in the transcript (Rose et al., abstract).
scored.rationale: If an explicit proposal and acceptance are decoded, the message is the agreement. Reliability is doubtful: decoding is shown in lab settings and the key must be established, and such handshakes are rare in emergent settings (2 of 229).

scored.title: Hidden channel detected, no agreement text recovered
scored.rationale: A channel shows secrecy or capacity, not what was agreed. A shared training history can produce the same code without any agreement (a focal point). Alternative state of T03: the two never occur in one case.

scored.title: Price-level audit finds supracompetitive prices
scored.as_reported: Any test whose input is a single agent's price or bid history has power exactly equal to its false-positive rate (abstract).
scored.rationale: The source shows that such audits are blind to this conduct by construction, so a positive or negative result carries no information about agreement.

scored.title: Excess residual correlation between agents' unexplained choices
scored.as_reported: Residual correlation of +0.053 between two deployments of one model against +0.0001 across models, across twenty models from nineteen developers (abstract).
scored.rationale: Detects coupling that price levels cannot, but the within-model excess is exactly what a shared model would produce, so it cannot separate agreement from common cause. Known confound, hence doubtful.

scored.title: Shared-model coupling as an alternative explanation of similar behaviour
scored.as_reported: Same measurement as T06, read in the other direction: similar behaviour arises between deployments of one model.
scored.rationale: The measurement is solid (twenty models, developer-clustered interval). It only undermines support that rests on similarity (T05, T06), not interventional support (T02). The demo has no alternative-explanation criterion, so it is entered as an exculpatory item and used only in cases where support is similarity-based.

scored.title: Internal-state probe shows the model recognises the true answer it does not report
scored.as_reported: Across eight models from five families the probe recovers the recognised answer at 0.70 to 0.87 balanced accuracy and stays readable under several forms of concealment (abstract).
scored.rationale: Reads knowledge of the true value directly, which is what the element 'knowledge, not error' asks for. Needs access to model internals and is a single preprint validated on open-weight models, hence doubtful. Source type M4 follows the pool; a mechanistic reading is closer to expert evidence.

scored.title: Reasoning-token count differs between truthful and untruthful answers
scored.as_reported: Three models answered 210 questions under prompts to answer truthfully, falsely or indifferently; truth-directed answers used fewer reasoning tokens. The authors state this does not yet establish a detector of spontaneous deception (abstract).
scored.rationale: The behaviour was prompted, not spontaneous, and the authors name the gap themselves. Records of reasoning may also not reflect the real cause.

scored.title: LLM judge reads the messages and reports collusion
scored.origin: own run, not archived in this repository
scored.as_reported: Project notes of 2026-10-23: on NARCBench steganographic runs the judge flagged 1 of 20 and 2 of 20 collusive runs against 0 of 20 controls (Fisher p about 1.0 and 0.49). Not reproduced here.
scored.report_element: E2 or E3 (verdict on the whole claim)
scored.rationale: A null result at n=20: the judge cannot be distinguished from zero. The judge's output is itself an inference from the messages. No element in the demo corresponds to a verdict on the whole claim.

scored.title: Sequence-level monitor detects structured misbehaviour that per-step monitors miss
scored.as_reported: On a synthetic marginal-preserving sabotage attack, a per-step monitor scores AUC 0.52 and sequence-level monitors 0.79 to 0.97 (abstract).
scored.rationale: The attack is a simulated construction on monitor scores, not real agent traces, and the result concerns detecting temporally structured misbehaviour, not whether the outcome differs from a world without collusion. The mapping to E4 follows the pool and is weak. The demo has no E4 element.

scored.pool_ref: plus factor: change of customer or trigger
scored.title: Same task for different customers: output quality differs
scored.as_reported: Project notes: US versus Chinese contractor persona 70% against 59% (p=0.03), ten comparisons without correction, none surviving Bonferroni at 0.005. Numbers not re-checked against the blog in this repository.
scored.report_element: adjacent: single-agent conditional conduct, not collusion
scored.rationale: A paired contrast shows that a trigger changes one model's conduct. It becomes evidence of agreement only when the manipulated variable is the partner agent (as in T01/T02), not the customer. Uncorrected multiple comparisons, hence doubtful.

excluded.title: Trace tampering
excluded.reason: A gate, not evidence. Abstract: all tested harnesses except one allowed agents to delete their traces when asked. Used as a sensitivity test on logged evidence (M2): lowering reliability or authenticity.

excluded.title: Economic intervention to break collusion
excluded.reason: A defence, not evidence. A refusal of a profitable deviation could be a 'contrary to self-interest' plus factor, but no such result was used.

excluded.title: Probe-the-object test and evidence confrontation
excluded.reason: Our protocols. No results exist yet, so they carry no weight.

excluded.title: Elicitation of hidden state
excluded.reason: Methods that induce the behaviour. They show susceptibility under induced conditions, not conduct in the case at hand.

excluded.title: Trajectory anomaly detectors
excluded.reason: Listed in the pool but not read beyond the title in this audit.
